When the Metropolitan Museum of Art ended pay-what-you-wish admission for out-of-state visitors in 2018, attendance barely moved. That fact is often cited as proof that fees do no harm. It proves something narrower: that tourists who have already flown to New York will pay twenty-five dollars for a museum.

The people a fee keeps out are the ones who were never going to be counted. A student from Queens who might have wandered in on a rainy afternoon does not appear in any attendance figure, because she never came. The galleries that benefit most from a free door is the ones nobody planned to visit.

A museum that charges to much has decided who its public is. It should at least say so.
